growth_problem: Paid search is getting more expensive while converting fewer evaluators. The loss concentrates on the pricing page, where paid search visitors increasingly leave without requesting a demo.

hypotheses.title: Unclear pricing is losing paid search evaluators
hypotheses.observed_problem: Paid search visitors exit the pricing page far more often than other traffic, fewer of them click through to a demo, and paid search acquisition cost has climbed.
hypotheses.affected_audience: Paid search evaluators, mostly small businesses, at the pricing step
hypotheses.causal_explanation: Evaluators cannot tell what each plan includes or what they would pay, so high-intent search visitors leave instead of requesting a demo.
hypotheses.intervention: A clearer plan comparison with explicit inclusions, usage limits, and an estimate of total cost.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Lower pricing-page exit rate and higher demo click-through for paid search traffic.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: More qualified demo requests per paid search dollar, bringing acquisition cost back down.

supporting.claim: Customers repeatedly say they cannot tell what plans include, and these comments are rising; one names arriving from a search ad.
Paid search exits on the pricing page are well above other sources and rising each month, with fewer demo clicks.
Paid search acquisition cost rose sharply as spend grew while wins fell.
Fewer paid search visits become leads than benchmark, consistent with evaluators leaving before converting.

missing: Pricing verbatims are not tagged by acquisition channel, so the paid search link rests on a few mentions.
No pricing-page survey or session recordings show which plan details confuse visitors.

hypotheses.title: Rising bids are buying lower-intent paid search traffic
hypotheses.observed_problem: Paid search spend rose while fewer of its leads qualify and fewer deals close.
hypotheses.affected_audience: Paid search visitors across the site
hypotheses.causal_explanation: Higher bids and broader keywords bring in price-shoppers with weaker intent.
hypotheses.intervention: Tighten keyword targeting and negative keywords for low-intent queries.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Higher lead-to-MQL conversion for paid search at similar volume.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: Lower acquisition cost through better traffic quality.

supporting.claim: Spend grew while wins fell, so each win costs more.
Paid search leads qualify less often than benchmark, which fits weaker intent.

contradicting.claim: The drop concentrates on the pricing page and in demo clicks there, which a site-wide traffic-quality shift would not predict.

missing: Search query and keyword mix reports over the period.

hypotheses.title: A broken mobile demo form loses ready-to-buy visitors
hypotheses.observed_problem: Mobile visitors start the demo form often but rarely finish it, rage-click, and wait on a slow page.
hypotheses.affected_audience: Mobile visitors on the demo page across channels
hypotheses.causal_explanation: A technical defect or slow script on the mobile demo page blocks form submission.
hypotheses.intervention: Profile and fix the mobile demo page and form, then verify completion tracking.
hypotheses.expected_behavior_change: Mobile demo-form completion rises toward the desktop rate.
hypotheses.expected_business_outcome: More demo requests and pipeline without additional spend.

supporting.claim: Mobile demo-form completion is far below desktop, with many more rage clicks and much slower loads.
Prospects report the demo form spinning or freezing on their phones.

missing: We cannot yet tell how many mobile starters later complete the form on desktop.
Server-side demo request counts by device would rule out a tracking gap.

action_detail: Run a pricing-page experiment for paid search traffic: a clear plan comparison with inclusions and usage limits against the current page, while a short intercept survey captures what visitors find unclear.
primary_metric: Demo requests per paid search pricing-page session.
guardrail_metric: Lead-to-SQL rate for paid search, so clearer pricing does not attract unqualified leads.
downstream_metric: Paid search acquisition cost and wins over the following quarter.
learning_objective: Learn whether pricing clarity, rather than traffic quality, drives the paid search decline.
missing_evidence: Paid search keyword and query mix over time.
